nodes.name: Modified Hummers' method
nodes.procedure: Graphene oxides (GOs) were synthesized following a modified Hummers' method, as previously established (23).

nodes.name: Hydrothermal sulfidation
nodes.procedure: An aqueous suspension of GO (1 mg ml⁻¹, 10 ml) was mixed with thiourea at a mass ratio of 1:50 (GO/thiourea), followed by sealing in a Teflon-lined stainless autoclave at 150°C for 3 hours to obtain HG.

nodes.name: Ni immobilization
nodes.procedure: Afterward, the as-obtained HG [6 to 7 mg; dispersed in 10 ml of N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF)] was mixed with 0.1 M Ni(acac)₂ (dissolved in 10 ml of DMF) at 80°C for 12 hours (1 atm) to form HG-Ni. The resultant HG-Ni was dispersed and stored in isopropanol with a concentration of 1 mg ml⁻¹.

nodes.name: Fe immobilization control
nodes.procedure: In a control experiment, we used the same procedure to synthesize an HG-Fe sample. In particular, HG (6 to 7 mg; in 10 ml of DMF) was mixed with 0.1 M Fe(acac)₃ (dissolved in 10 ml of DMF) at 80°C for 12 hours (1 atm).

nodes.description: OER performance in 1 M KOH glass cell
nodes.source_text: Cyclic voltammetry (CV) of HG-Ni was conducted in 1 M KOH using common glassware as the electrochemical cell (Fig. 2A and fig. S6). In the initial scan, the HG-Ni showed a pair of redox peaks at 1.3 to 1.4 V [all potentials were quoted against the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) unless stated otherwise], corresponding to the typical Ni²⁺/³⁺ couple (36-38). At higher potentials, HG-Ni delivered an insignificant OER current.

nodes.description: OER performance in purified 1 M KOH plastic vessel
nodes.source_text: CV of HG-Ni was conducted in a purified KOH solution without Fe species in a plastic vessel. The redox currents of Ni²⁺/³⁺ exhibited little variation, and OER currents remained small during the CV cycles (Fig. 2B).

nodes.description: iR-compensated LSV OER performance comparison HG-NiFe vs HG-NiFe_x
nodes.source_text: To reduce the influence of metal redox and the capacitance currents of HG-NiFe on OER activity, we conducted linear scanning voltammogram (LSV) at a low scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹ in 1 M KOH, and the iR-corrected polarization curve was collected (Fig. 3A). HG-NiFe afforded an OER onset potential of 1.54 V (defined as the potential at 10 mA cm⁻²)... At η = 0.35 V, the TOF was calculated to be 0.53 s⁻¹.

nodes.description: Faradaic efficiency O2 detection by GC in H-type cell
nodes.source_text: The OER products on HG-NiFe were analyzed by gas chromatography (fig. S8). O₂ was the only gaseous product and it was produced with Faradic efficiencies (FEs) of 100% at potentials from 1.54, 1.58, and 1.62, to 1.66 V.

nodes.description: CV with varying FeCl3 concentrations 2.4-12 μM in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: With the increase in the content of FeCl3 from 2.4 to 12 μM, the improvement was observed to be significant initially and then gradually turned to be very moderate (Fig. 2, C and D).
In addition, long-term measurement indicated the good stability of HG-NiFe for OER electrocatalysis (fig. S9).

nodes.description: Comparative LSV OER performance in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: HG-NiFe afforded an OER onset potential of 1.54 V (defined as the potential at 10 mA cm⁻²), whereas the value was 1.6 V on HG-NiFe_x. Correspondingly, the Tafel slope increased from 39 to 59 mV dec⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show two-dimensional HG-Ni structures with substantial wrinkles and scrolls characteristic of graphene; no crystal lattices of Ni oxides observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscope (TEM) images showed that the two-dimensional HG-Ni structures contained substantial wrinkles and scrolls, which were the characteristics of graphene ... On the graphene layers, the crystal lattices of Ni oxides were not observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX spectroscopy indicates clear and uniform distribution of Ni in HG-Ni at molecular scales; Ni signal not detected on HG precursor.
nodes.evidence_snippet: However, energy-dispersive x-ray (EDX) spectroscopy indicated a clear and uniform distribution of Ni, implying that the Ni sites in HG-Ni could be at molecular scales ... The Ni signal was not detected on the HG precursor by EDX.

nodes.characterization_summary: Normalized Ni K-edge XAS of HG-Ni shows slightly increased pre-edge peak intensity compared to Ni(acac)2, indicating similar distorted octahedral coordination geometry; pre-edge energy shift ~0.08 eV reflects equivalent ligand field; Ni oxidation state +2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From Ni(acac)2 to HG-Ni, the pre-edge peak of Ni sites only increased slightly, suggesting the similar coordination geometry of Ni sites in Ni(acac)2 and HG-Ni ... the pre-edge energy shifted very slightly [~0.08 eV from Ni(acac)2 to HG-Ni] ... Based on the rising-edge energy, the oxidation state of Ni sites (+2) in HG-Ni was barely altered.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier-transformed Ni K-edge EXAFS shows minor increase in Ni-O bond length; significant change in outer shell at R' of 2.68 Å confirming bonding of Ni2+ ions with HG.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Fourier-transformed extended x-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS; Fig. 1C) analysis, the bond length of the inner shell of Ni centers (that is, Ni-O bonds) showed a minor increase. However, the outer shell changed significantly based on the peak at a radial distance (R′) of 2.68 Å, confirming the bonding of Ni2+ ions with HG.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR spectra exhibit characteristic vibration of Ni(acac)2 at 2990 cm−1 shifted to 2973 cm−1 in HG-Ni, supporting molecular Ni sites without decomposition to Ni oxides.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform infrared (FTIR; fig. S4) spectra exhibited a characteristic vibration of Ni(acac)2 at 2990 cm−1. This characteristic vibration was caused by its methylene groups. The FTIR signal of the methylene groups on the HG-Ni was also observed at 2973 cm−1.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images reveal graphene structure of HG-NiFe; no Ni/Fe hydroxides or oxides observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images revealed the graphene structure of HG-NiFe, and the EDX results indicated the uniform distribution of Ni and Fe on the graphene layers ... None of the Ni/Fe hydroxides (or oxides) were observed in HG-NiFe.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX indicates uniform distribution of Ni and Fe on graphene layers in HG-NiFe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images revealed the graphene structure of HG-NiFe, and the EDX results indicated the uniform distribution of Ni and Fe on the graphene layers.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern of HG-NiFe shows only graphite (002) and (111) facets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The x-ray diffraction pattern showed only the graphite (002) and (111) facets.

nodes.characterization_summary: Normalized Ni K-edge XAS shows no difference in pre-edge and rising-edge positions between HG-Ni and HG-NiFe, indicating unchanged coordination geometry and oxidation state of Ni sites upon Fe incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: On the basis of the normalized Ni K-edge XAS analysis, we found that there was almost no difference in the pre-edge and rising-edge positions of the Ni sites between HG-Ni and HG-NiFe.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier-transformed Ni K-edge EXAFS of HG-NiFe shows significantly increased peak with R' shifting to ~2.71 Å compared to HG-Ni; Fe K-edge EXAFS shows intense peak at R' = 2.72 Å, confirming Fe bonded at neighboring Ni sites with Ni-Fe distance ~2.7 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The local structure of the Ni sites was investigated using EXAFS (Fig. 4B). The significantly increased peak was observed with R′ slightly shifting around 2.71 Å. This indicated that the outer shell of the Ni centers in HG-NiFe obviously changed compared to that of HG-Ni ... The outer shell of the Fe centers was identified by the intense peak at R′ = 2.72 Å. This is consistent with the one collected at the Ni centers, reflecting that Fe was bonded at the neighboring sites of Ni centers in HG-NiFe.
